correctness.rationale: Work at fixed 0<b<1/2 and reflect for b>1/2. In log-odds coordinates g=y+a(X-b), with critical points ±c_a and c_a=log a+O(a^-1). The right inverse roots of ±c_a lie beyond ab/2 for large a; their defining identity first gives y=ab±c_a+o(1), and then X(y)=O_b(a exp(-ab)). The middle inverse roots lie in a fixed compact interval: testing bounded y on either side of h(2b) and h(b) brackets them, and g's defining identity gives the stated endpoint errors. The decreasing interval covers both intervals; the increasing interval covers only the decreasing one. Every admissible two-letter cylinder has a derivative product bounded below by a constant times a, so inverse cylinders shrink, all words are realized uniquely, and a fixed-a smooth coordinate change transfers uniform expansion in the iterate sense. For pairs 00,01,10 the physical coordinate estimates follow respectively from both log-odds coordinates bounded, the next coordinate near ab, and the present coordinate near ab. Invariance gives masses 1-2q,q,q exactly. Pairwise coupling yields W1, integration of the bounded log-odds coboundary gives exact mean b, and the Lipschitz variance integrand gives the uniform variance error. In log-odds coordinates the same pair classes give log a+log[b(1-b)], log a+log[2b(1-2b)], and zero to the required error. The conjugacy derivative changes the integral only by a bounded coboundary for each fixed a. Stationary Markov measures realize every q and are ergodic for interior q and at the two periodic endpoints. The cyclic word (10)^m followed by n-2m zeros realizes each rational m/n≤1/2, proving periodic density of limiting pairs. Conditioning entropy on one preceding symbol bounds it by the displayed H(q), with equality for the Markov law. Maximization gives q=1/(φ²+1) and H=log φ. The physical-variance interpretation is asymptotic, not an equality at a specified finite-a variance.
residual_risks: Uniformity is in the invariant law at each fixed asymmetric b. Expansion is uniform over iterates on the specified subsystem, not a claim of one-step physical expansion at every point.

value.rationale: The fixed mean was known, but it conceals large differences between stationary laws. A uniform coupling of the entire physical marginal, jointly with a two-term Lyapunov law and a sharp physical interpretation of entropy, resolves a natural question about what the subsystem's coding actually means for observables. The frequency distinguishes the whole limiting family rather than only one natural measure or a few periodic orbits.
residual_risks: The result concerns one subsystem and does not describe general invariant laws of the ambient interval, finite-parameter entropy at a prescribed physical variance, or the symmetric limit.
